title: Least Privilege
briefing: Case #3. This agent's only job is "summarize my calendar for tomorrow", and the poisoned weather_lookup tool from Case #2 is installed on it too. You can't remove the tool, but you can remove permissions. Use /revoke <scope> until the attack can't succeed, then /replay. The calendar summary must still work. /start restores all scopes.
teaching: Excessive agency means an agent holds more permissions, tools or autonomy than its task needs, so any successful manipulation can do more damage. Least privilege limits the blast radius: even a fully hijacked agent can only do what its scopes allow. A data-theft attack generally needs two capabilities, a way to read the secret and a way to send it out, and removing either one breaks the chain. General-purpose capabilities like a shell often provide both at once.

trace.text: Loaded MCP tools: calendar_list, weather_lookup (same server as Case #2).

scopes.description: Make HTTP requests to any host.

hints: The attack needs two things: a way to read the key and a way to send it out.
Some scopes can do both jobs at once.
Ask of each scope: does summarizing a calendar need this?
lesson: Grant each agent the minimum scopes for its task. Never give network egress to an agent that can read secrets, and treat shells as both a read and an exfil channel.
